pr_title: kernel: mem_domain: test max available partitions on add_partition
pr_body:
- Add an __ASSERT() test in k_mem_domain_add_partition() to check for available slots
- clean up the to ensure the test_mem_part_assert_add_overmax() clears the need_recover_spinlock flag to avoid future test failures.

Fixes: zephyrproject-rtos#34911

Signed-off-by: David Leach <david.leach@nxp.com>

I don't quite understand how this test_mem_part_assert_add_overmax() test case is supposed to work. It is using a mix of MPU driver code and kernel code to fiddle with partitions. When it makes a call to arch_mem_domain_max_partitions_get() to get the maximum number of partitions this function is for the platform and in the case of the NXP core it returns a value that also removes the static partitions from the real memory map (including reserving parts for stack guards for supervisor and thread stacks). So by the time this test case is run, the partitions_get() returns a value of 4. 

But the test case is using a locally defined  struct k_mem_domain test_domain structure to play with partitions. This structure has an array for the number of partitions set to CONFIG_MAX_DOMAIN_PARTITIONS which is 16. So the call to k_mem_domain_add_partition() will return true because only 4 of the entries are used and as such the particular test case fails. 

I suspect these tests were originally written for x86 where ARCH_MEM_DOMAIN_SYNCHRONOUS_API is true which would force a synchronous update of the added partition and thus give an immediate error to k_mem_domain_add_partition(). The NXP cores don't use this setting and because the kernel function doesn't have any insight on what is really available from the SOC MPU it will happily add the partition.

I don't know how this behaves on non-NXP ARM cores but I'm thinking it may be the same thing.

As for the original reason for this bug ticket, test_kobject_perm_error fails because the previous failed memory test, test_mem_part_assert_add_overmax(), did not fault as expected so the variable need_recover_spinlock used to release the z_mem_domain_lock spinlock is still set. So when the first test case in kobject_perm faults, the after fault handler thinks it needs to reset the z_mem_domain_lock spinlock and gets a kernel assert because it doesn't own the lock.

I can add a reset of the variable but this leaves the earlier problem with test_mem_part_assert_add_overmax() still not working as expected on these boards.
To get the NXP style MPU to detect a overmax() condition, you have to have the thread owning the memory domain to be running. Then when the swap tries to load up the partitions it will fail.

wait, I know during my debugging that I saw this value be something else because the underlying drivers for the NXP MPU had not been run yet to set the static_regions_num that is subtracted from the number of available regions. So the initial value would be 9 then after running it would be 4. 

But now I've just pulled, again, from the tip of master and the case is no longer failing when it was this morning and last night.

Do we have a race condition for when init_mem_domain_module() is called and when the MPU driver may get run to set the static fields?

hm... `init_mem_domain_module()` is called via `SYS_INIT()` at `PRE_KERNEL_1`. This should be after the call to `arch_kernel_init()` in `arch/arm/include/aarch32/kernel_arch_func.h` where it calls `z_arm_mpu_init()`.
`static_regions_num` is updated via `mpu_configure_static_mpu_regions()`. Maybe this is why?

No we don't. Given the PR I referenced above moved the initialization of the mpu_configure_static_mpu_regions() to occur before the PRE_KERNEL_1 initialization of the kernel/mem_domain.c:init_mem_domain_module() the variable in question is now initialized before being referenced.
